findings.claim: The footnote's extent (end offset) is published and documented (ADR-031 §c step 3 / §g: 402285–402521, 236 chars; case provenance) but no gate check pins it — the `evidence` anchor only asserts containment, and the `evidence` key is silently ignored by every other check type, so a wrong footnote slice passes the case.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py:88-98 (text_contains only; `max_chars`/`text_not_contains` at :97-110 never read chk['evidence']). In-memory: evidence.footnote end ±1, or replaced by item 14's whole span {402235,402556} -> case green. Breaking `segment.PARA_END_RE` (never matches) makes `footnote_pointer` return (72070, 414197) — a DIFFERENT `*`-led line, 342,127 chars — and `ba-2003-asterisk-ibr` still passes 19/19. `{'type':'max_chars','item':'11','evidence':'footnote','value':100}` returns None (236 > 100) and `{'type':'text_not_contains','item':'11','evidence':'footnote','value':'proxy statement'}` returns None — both silently check the span instead.
findings.repro: python3 -B -c "import sys,json,re;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.sec10k import segment;from src.sec10k.eval_adapter import run_case;segment.PARA_END_RE=re.compile(r'(?!x)x');print(run_case(json.load(open('evals/adversarial/ba-2003-asterisk-ibr.json')))['passed'])"  # True
findings.acceptance: A gate check that goes red when evidence.footnote's extent is wrong (e.g. `max_chars` honouring `evidence`, or an exact-offsets/evidence-length check pinning 236 chars on items 11 and 13), watched red under the PARA_END_RE mutation; and either the other span check types honour `evidence` or the adapter refuses an `evidence` key on a check type that does not read it.

findings.claim: Two of the rule's three conjuncts (same asterisk run on the heading; footnote names THIS code) are pinned only by `segment._demo`, not by any fast/invariant case — removing the marker guard flips nothing on all 47 documents, so the gate cannot see it.
findings.evidence: In-memory mutation appending `*` to every heading_text before `footnote_pointer` -> zero status changes on 47 docs, ba-2003-asterisk-ibr green. Only `_demo` (run by ci.yml, not by the eval gate) asserts the `**` vs `*` and not-named cases (src/sec10k/segment.py:862-867). ADR-031 §b4 'each is pinned (§h)' is true only via the self-check.
findings.repro: in-memory wrapper on extract.footnote_pointer appending '*' to every heading -> run_case passed True
findings.acceptance: Either ADR-031 §b4/§h say explicitly that the marker-run and named-code conjuncts are pinned by the CI self-check only (no corpus instance can pin them), or a derived fixture pins one of them in the gate.

findings.claim: `ITEM_LIST_RE` reads a dotted or parenthesised sub-item reference as a top-level code ('Item 5.03 of Form 8-K' names '5'; 'Item 15(b)'/'Item 15(a)(3)' name '15'), which ADR-031 §i does not list; harmless on the corpus but a false-positive surface the not-claimed list omits.
findings.evidence: ITEM_LIST_RE on 'Item 5.03 of Form 8-K' -> {'5'}; axp-2008@326904 and xom-2021@385888 are two of the census's 11 non-external lines that carry this shape.
findings.repro: python3 -B -c "import sys,re;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.sec10k.segment import ITEM_LIST_RE;print(ITEM_LIST_RE.findall('pursuant to Item 5.03 of Form 8-K'))"
findings.acceptance: Either `\d{1,2}[A-D]?\b(?![.(])` (or equivalent) in ITEM_LIST_RE with a `_demo` line, or one sentence in ADR-031 §i naming sub-item references as not guarded.
